statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online name certification portal (www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (denominación social) must be expressed in Castilian Spanish or in a co-official autonomous community language with Spanish; foreign words must be transliterated into Latin script and adapted to Spanish phonetics; the name must not be contrary to law, morality, or public order, must not misrepresent the corporate type or business activity, and must not be identical or phonetically/visually confusingly similar to names already registered; an SL must end with 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada', 'S.L.', 'Sociedad Limitada', or 'SL'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Ministerio, Gobierno, Rey, Reina, Príncipe, Corona
Oficial, Nacional, Organismo, Administración Pública, Agencia Estatal, Real
Banco, Caja, Seguros, Reaseguros, Financiera (reserved for regulated financial entities subject to prior Bank of Spain / SEPBLAC authorization)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., Sociedad Comanditaria, Sociedad Cooperativa (corporate type tokens inconsistent with the SL form)
Terms falsely describing the activity, such as Customs, Aduana, Bonded, Transporte Internacional, when the corresponding license or authorization is not yet held
Geographic indicators, including Madrid, Barcelona, España, or foreign jurisdiction names, where their use may mislead the public without proper authority
Tokens requiring prior ministerial approval under the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996) and RMC administrative criteria
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A favorable negative name certification (certificación negativa de denominación social) is valid for 90 days and may be renewed by re-filing a new application before the Registro Mercantil Central; upon rejection, the applicant receives written grounds and may either re-file with a corrected name or file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month pursuant to Articles 121 and 122 of Ley 39/2015; a further contentious-administrative appeal before the Audiencia Nacional remains available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may serve only as a supplementary correspondence address; the registered office (domicilio social) must be a physically real address within Spanish territory where the SL is effectively administered, per Article 9 of Ley 1/2010. For the ISIC 5222 customs-bonded truck fleet activity, the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) customs authorization (authorized economic operator status or bonded transport operator authorization under the Union Customs Code) requires verifiable operational premises, fleet records, GPS-seal infrastructure, and demonstrative commercial substance; therefore a purely virtual office is insufficient for this industry and will not satisfy the customs substance test.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 60% within the first 12 months of operation and over 85% within the first 3 years, driven by AEAT customs external audit cycles, SEPBLAC AML/CFT inspection programs, and Guardia Civil oversight of bonded transport operations; unannounced physical inspections may occur simultaneously at the registered office and fleet depot.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 4 and 33 (minimum share capital), Article 20 (incorporation deed), Article 21 (registration), Article 22 (BORME publication), Article 60 (full-paid capital requirement), Articles 209-211 and 215 (registered office and directors); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, RRM), Articles 135-145 and 324-328 (inscription and appeals); Ley 14/2013 (digital incorporation via CIRCE); Real Decreto 1427/1989 (registry tariff scale).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (negative name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (inscription of the deed); Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (definitive NIF); Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (statutory publication).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) granted before a Spanish Notary and filed as 'primera copia' for inscription in the company's hoja registral.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000 under Article 4.2 LSC. The capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind at incorporation (Article 60 LSC); cash contributions must be deposited in a bank account opened in the company's name with an authorized Spanish credit institution and evidenced by a bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the Notary. No separate escrow account is required by law; the deposit is released upon registration. Note: although the input metadata flags 'minimum_capital_requirement' as false, Spanish law is mandatory and no notary or registrar will form an SL with capital below EUR 3,000. For this bonded fleet entity, subscribed capital of EUR 3,100 is recommended, and the transport licensing regime separately supports this with a first-vehicle financial capacity requirement of EUR 9,000 under EU Regulation 1071/2009.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - 1. Ratification. The incorporation deed of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, granted before the competent Spanish Notary, is ratified, and the company's separate legal personality is acknowledged as effective upon inscription in the Mercantile Registry. 2. Capital. The subscription and full payment of the share capital of EUR 3,100 is recorded and confirmed. 3. Registered Office. The registered office at [Address], Madrid, Spain, is adopted as the statutory seat, tax domicile, and venue for the shareholders' meeting. 4. Appointments. [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Único), and [Name] is appointed Secretary (non-director), with authority to obtain the definitive NIF, open bank accounts, and execute all regulatory filings.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic offices at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; VAT-specific portal accessed via Sistemas de Información del IVA (SII) web services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SL in formation: (1) apply to AEAT for a provisional NIF (Form 036 or via notary) before executing the incorporation deed; (2) execute deed before a notary and register the SL in the Mercantile Registry; (3) file Form 036/037 to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF (9-character CIF format: alphabetic prefix, 8 digits, check digit); (4) register for VAT in the same censal census, obtaining the NIF-IVA (ES + 9 characters); (5) if making intra-Community supplies, also enroll in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) via Form 036; (6) non-resident shareholders need no local NIF for holding purposes but directors/representatives require an appointment-of-representative filing and, where applicable, an NIF-ES for the non-resident entity if it supplies goods/services, with all filings performed digitally using an electronic certificate (certificado digital/FNMT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Spanish tax-resident SLs are taxed on worldwide income in the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at the standard 25% rate, with no pass-through attribution to shareholders; no check-the-box exists, and the SL is per se a corporation; branches of foreign entities are entity-level taxed on Spanish-source income with a 25% rate (spect the absence of territorial exemption), and the Canary Islands ZEC zone grants a reduced 4% IS rate and territorial concessions for qualifying operations but does not alter the Entity_Level_Taxation default classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists; available elections and optional regimes under national law: (a) reduced 15% IS rate for qualifying 'empresa emergente' startups (Law 28/2022) for the first two profitable periods (base capped); (b) optional consolidated tax group regime (art. 100 LIS) requiring 75%+ direct/indirect ownership, Spanish-resident parent and subsidiaries, filed with IS 311000/AEAT; (c) VAT group regime (Régimen especial de grupo de entidades) under art. 62 octies LIVA for wholly-owned VAT groups; (d) cash-basis VAT regime (Régimen de caja) for SMEs with turnover ≤ €2,000,000 invoicing other cash-basis taxpayers; (e) simplified VAT regime (Régimen simplificado) for enumerated small activities with turnover below €250,000/€125,000, elected annually; (f) anti-hybrid notifications under Law 5/2022 (ATAD 1 & 2) apply by default with no election; (g) optional Spanish GAAP 'método de integración' for currency translations are accounting elections not tax identity elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) - Value Added Tax harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, Ley 37/1992, Real Decreto 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-activity exemption threshold: any taxable person performing taxable supplies of goods or services in Spain must register (Form 036/037) before commencing activity. De minimis concessions are limited to (i) the simplified regime (turnover ≤ €250,000 in the prior year for listed activities) and (ii) cash-basis VAT (≤ €2,000,000), neither of which relieves the duty to become a registered VAT taxpayer. Non-established foreign suppliers effecting distance sales or 3PL/warehouse operations likewise register via Form 036 without turnover threshold, subject to the simplified one-stop-shop (OSS/IOSS) alternative for distance sales with applicable EU €10,000/€100,000 dispatch thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for all entrepreneurs and professionals from 2025 (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece'; private B2B obligation entered into force after implementing regulation is issued, with the public-sector Facturae e-invoicing regime already binding since 2015 for suppliers to Government). For large taxpayers (turnover > €6,000,000), real-time fiscal clearance via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires, within 4 calendar days after the invoice becomes registrable (8 days inclusive of extension), transmission of structured VAT invoice/record data (Field-by-Field XML) using SOAP/Web Service APIs (G2G attachments: L0801-Facturas, L0901/B, etc.), and submittance of annual G4/G5 book-electronic records; SII entities cannot use the simplified ledger and must file monthly VIES. In addition, the Verifactu bill-validation system (RD 1007/2023) obliges billing software to produce one-way hash-chained records and, where integrated in the SII, marks invoices with a 'QR' stamp, while non-SII taxpayers must provide an 'end-to-end' XML verification mechanism and standard invoice metadata; failure to integrate e-invoicing APIs or keep Verifactu-compliant logic triggers VAT-invoice-issuance penalties (up to €1,000 per invoice, aggregate caps under LGT art. 200).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated (exempt with credit) supplies: (a) definitive exports of goods dispatched outside the EU/ECTA (art. 21.1 LIVA) where the shipper obtains and preserves proof of exit within the statutory period; (b) intra-Community supplies (EDI) to a customer holding a valid NIF-IVA, recorded in the VIES register of operators, provided the supplier files periodic VIES (£303/390) and the goods physically move within the EU (art. 25 LIVA); (c) transport of goods to third countries or the Community, and ancillary services (loading/unloading, customs clearance, bonded warehousing) physically rendered in facilitation of an export/import movement (art. 23 LIVA) - the bond truck feeder service between an EU airport and a customs-sealed transit hub qualifies where the transport itinerary is to/from a third-country destination and is evidenced in the CMR/airwaybill; (d) services directly linked to exported goods recharged to the exporter (art. 22.2 LIVA) when consumed in Spain but occasioned by the export; (e) B2B services supplied to non-established customers are zero-rated by destination rule (reverse charge in the customer country) under art. 5?? place-of-supply rules; However, the zero-rating requires the exporter to be the owner of the transit operation, to have valid EORI/TIN for customs declarations, and to observe the strict documentary evidence required by art. 21.2/24 LIVA and the Tarifas for 'depósitos aduaneros' where goods are declared to the 'Régimen de tránsito externo'.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA - Documento Único Administrativo (Single Administrative Document) incorporating the electronic export declaration in the Sistema Aduanero (e.D.T./ABA/CTTI), including the EORI number and the corresponding conditional exit confirmations
Exit proof (Justificante de salida de las mercancías - Cédula de despacho / confirmación del Puesto de Inspección de Frontera, stating the date of actual dispatch from EU territory)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (Conocimiento de embarque or Master House Airwaybill) evidencing the goods' routing
CMR consignment note (Carta de Porte por Carretera) for the bonded truck fleet operations showing destination, cargo count, seal number and customs seals intact
T1/T2 transit declaration or internal transit document (e-MRN via NCTS) where the bonded movement is under Union transit
Commercial invoice (Factura comercial) aligning description, value and Incoterms with the DUA

Inward Remittance Certificate (Justificante de cobro / certificado bancario de remesa de entrada de divisas or SWIFT MT103 / NIGE code from Banco de España Foreign Transaction Reporting) demonstrating the export price has been collected
Bank/telex evidence of payment within the reputed six-month repatriation window; for foreign currency billing the exchange rate must match the DUA customs value
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate physical exit, compliance with customs seals (precinto), or preserved documentation within the prescription window (4 years general; 5 years where declarations omitted; up to 10 years for certain non-transparent offshore structures) triggers retrospective VAT recharacterization at 21% plus late-payment interest (3.75% recargo de apremio escalating to 5% + 2% surcharge after 12 months, and up to 20% additional charge where the assessment is administrative). Export fraud or 'falsa exportación' penalties: tax-infraction fines of 50%-150% of the VAT improperly zero-rated (art. 191/193 LGT), nonlinear for repeated conduct; documentary inaccuracy penalties up to €15,000 (art. 198 LGT) per omission; Mekong? separate customs infraction fines for illegal export (up to 3 x customs value and disqualifications). Criminal tax fraud (art. 305 CP) applies where defrauded VAT exceeds €120,000, with imprisonment and fines up to 6x the defrauded amount and removal of zero-rating plus recharge of VAT from customers (the exporter remains liable and is barred from issuing corrective credit notes). The AEAT also applies the 'loss of the right to deduction' and cumulative clawback of input VAT previously reclaimed for the goods/services underlying the false export, with a statutory obligation to notify changes in proofs (FAU/Exports under art. 21 LIVA, resolutions ESE).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member state with full liberalization of both capital and current accounts under EU law. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted subject to 19% dividend withholding tax and CRS/FATCA reporting. Hurdles for non-EU owners include beneficial ownership verification and source-of-funds attestation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts must be repatriated to a Spanish resident bank account within six months of shipment date. Mandatory conversion to EUR; commercial documentation required to evidence transaction nature.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Permitted under MiCA and Spanish AML directives; fintech EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business) support Spanish IBANs with local account linkage required for full compliance and transaction monitoring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via Cl@ve PIN or video KYC permitted for Spanish SL entities; physical director appearance required only for transactions above €100,000 or enhanced due diligence triggers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership disclosure or complex ownership structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized beneficial ownership certificate, Registro Mercantil extract, and source-of-wealth evidence
Full KYC package including passport copies, proof of address, and PEP declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 transfers with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification via beneficial ownership filings, source-of-funds statements, and BOE registry extracts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for settlements; Commercial Letters of Credit via correspondent banks. Bonded truck operations require integration with customs declarations (ATA Carnet, TIR) for compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts, management report where applicable, and statutory audit report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the usual filing deadline is 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may begin after one year from the filing deadline, preventing registration of most company documents. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 and may reach EUR 300,000 for companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company, the usual deadline is 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax payable generally triggers a fixed penalty of EUR 100, or EUR 200 after a Tax Agency request. Tax payable may trigger late-filing surcharges of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months, and 15% thereafter, plus applicable interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration or confirmation accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts. Beneficial ownership information must also be updated promptly when ownership or control changes; the annual filing should confirm current information or report changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry compliance issues, and potential sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering legislation, including significant administrative fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, net annual turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of more than 50 employees. Audit obligations also arise for certain regulated, public-interest, subsidized, securities-market, or group circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad), with applicable Spanish commercial and accounting regulations. IFRS applies principally to consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply where legally elected or otherwise required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owners and control structure. The annual accounts filing includes the required beneficial ownership declaration or confirmation. Any change in ownership, voting rights, or control must be recorded in the corporate records and reflected in the relevant registry filings without waiting for the next annual filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, where applicable
Beneficial ownership information and supporting control documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,650 annually for a standard registered-office and corporate-secretarial service, excluding additional filings and correspondence handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 for a small Spanish SL subject to statutory audit; complex, regulated, or high-volume logistics businesses may cost more

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) under Ley 27/2014, Article 29.1
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created SLs with active economic activities may apply 15% on taxable base up to EUR 300,000 and 20% on the excess, for the first two tax periods with positive taxable base under Article 29.2 LIS, subject to substance conditions. Reduced rates also apply to credit unions, pension funds, and certain regulated investment vehicles. Standard 25% rate applies to a customs bonded truck fleet operator unless the two-year new-company regime is validly claimed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited under Article 26 LIS; annual offset of carried-forward losses is capped at 70% of pre-offset taxable base for taxpayers with net turnover of at least EUR 20 million, 80% for turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million, and 100% for turnover below EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Corporate Income Tax Annual Return; filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electronica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) with XBRL/XML attachments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year SLs the deadline is 1 to 25 July. A non-calendar fiscal year ending on 31 March requires filing by 25 September, and so on.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, legal name, corporate form SL, registered office, and registry data of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's Spanish NIF. Non-resident parent references must not be used in this box; foreign shareholder details are reported in the annual information return Modelo 232 where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact dates of the corporate income tax period, which must correspond to the financial statements filed and the board's annual accounts approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The period must coincide with the Spanish statutory accounts. A mismatch with the parent's consolidated period does not alter the Spanish filing obligation and may trigger automatic inspections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box [20] Net turnover (importe neto de la cifra de negocios)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross invoicing for bonded road feeder services, customs seal operations, airport freight handling, and ancillary logistics, reduced by returns, discounts, and VAT (if any).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All non-EUR amounts must be converted at the AEAT official annual exchange rate. Intra-group services invoiced to non-resident entities must be at arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted by permanent and temporary differences, prior-year loss offset, capitalisation reserve, and tax-free goodwill allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses recharged by the non-resident parent, management fees, and royalty charges are taxable adjustments unless they meet the benefit, business purpose, and bookkeeping requirements of Article 15 LGT and transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box [125] Tax payable / settlement (cuota íntegra / resultante)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final annual amount of IS after deductions, double-taxation reliefs, withholding taxes, and quarterly instalment payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty/DTA relief is not applied in this box by the Spanish company; withholding taxes and refunds for non-resident shareholders are handled separately under the IRNR procedure, supported by Form 296 and tax residence certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers the Article 27 LGT extemporaneous surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. If the return shows zero amount due, a fixed penalty of EUR 200 typically applies; if the AEAT required the filing, Article 198 LGT penalties may reach EUR 20,000. Incorrect or incomplete returns may be penalised up to EUR 3,300 or 2% of the amount if misreported.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 - Corporate Income Tax Quarterly Instalment Payment; filed electronically through AEAT Sede Electronica. Consolidated groups use Modelo 222.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (three instalment periods per fiscal year for calendar-year taxpayers: April, October, December)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 1 to 20 April for the first quarter, 1 to 20 October for the second quarter, and 1 to 20 December for the third quarter. For non-calendar fiscal years, each instalment is due within 20 days after the quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit after tax, based on the financial statements of the immediately preceding completed fiscal year, adjusted for instalment purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish entity must use Spanish statutory accounting profit; eliminating foreign parent IFRS adjustments keeps the calculation procedurally valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, deductions for double taxation, bonus reductions, and any applicable new-company reduced-rate relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only credits available under Spanish law may be deducted; foreign tax credits from a non-resident parent cannot be flowed through the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base of the instalment calculated using the statutory percentage method (18% of adjusted accounting profit for 2024) or the discretion of the taxpayer in certain cases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border bonded trucking groups, the instalment must reflect intercompany thin capitalisation and TP adjustments already known at quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting quarterly prepayment to the Spanish tax authority after reduction for withholding and other prepayments already paid by the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalment payments are credits against the annual Modelo 200 liability; they do not reduce obligations of non-resident shareholders in respect of Spanish WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For failure to pay or late payment of Modelo 202 instalments, Article 27 LGT surcharge plus late interest applies. Failure to file may be penalised under Article 198 LGT with a minimum EUR 200 per form; inaccurate presentments may be sanctioned at 10% of the tax amount, subject to the provisions on voluntary correction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, Ley 5/2004) on dividends distributed by the Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder not acting through a Spanish permanent establishment. 0% may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the non-resident corporate shareholder holds at least 5% of the SL's capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period and meets substance conditions. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% depending on shareholding and residence jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder claiming DTA or EU Directive relief must: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the home jurisdiction for the relevant calendar year; (2) register with Spanish tax authorities through the non-resident NIF procedure; (3) deliver the TRC, shareholder ownership certificate, and any treaty-required statement of beneficial ownership to the Spanish SL before the distribution date; and (4) if the full 19% is withheld, file Form 210 (non-resident income tax return) with the AEAT requesting a refund of the excess WHT within four years. The Spanish entity must file Modelo 216 (withholding tax declaration for non-residents) and Modelo 296 (annual information form) when distributions are made to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR WHT on interest is 19% and on royalty payments to non-residents is 24% generally (19% for beneficiaries resident in an EU/EEA state with effective exchange of information). Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, qualifying associated companies resident in the EU may benefit from 0% WHT on interest and royalties subject to a minimum 25% holding period of two years (or equivalent conditions). Treaty rates vary, typically 0%-10% for interest and 5%-10% for royalties, but permanent establishment for tax purposes of the non-resident in Spain loses treaty entitlement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover for the Spanish Local File; the Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated net turnover exceeds EUR 45,000,000. De minimis exemptions apply to individual related-party transactions of less than EUR 250,000 per category and counterparty, provided the taxpayer does not meet the materiality threshold. In practice, a customs bonded truck fleet SL with non-resident parent recharges must prepare full TP documentation if its net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million or group consolidated revenues exceed EUR 45 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like the UAE or BVI. However, Spanish tax law applies a modified substance-over-form doctrine through the general anti-abuse rule (Article 15 LGT), the substance and business-purpose requirements of Article 13.2 LIS, CFC rules (Articles 100-108 LIS), beneficial-ownership requirements in DTAs, and the MLI's principal-purpose test. A Spanish SL operating GPS-sealed bonded trucks for airport freight must demonstrate operational management, physical premises, local employees, service contracts, transport licences, customs bonds, and business risk in Spain. Insufficient substance will trigger recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, deemed dividend treatment, and TP adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of freight revenues, overstatement of deductible expenses, issuing false invoices from shell suppliers, destroying GPS and customs seal logs, or under-declaring the Spanish tax base by more than EUR 120,000 per tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the defrauded amount under Article 191 LGT, plus surcharge and late interest. If the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Article 305 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount. Amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 are aggravated and may lead to higher prison terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for tax debts caused by their negligent or intentional failure to comply (Article 42 LGT). Individual managers who approved falsified freight records can be indicted as participants in tax fraud, face embargo of personal assets, judicial travel bans, disqualification from running companies, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing intercompany invoices for bonded trucking services, management fees, or GPS data licences below arm's length prices; shifting profit to low-tax non-resident entities by unjustified commissions; failing to maintain contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation; or entering into circular routes designed to reduce Spanish taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate income tax adjustment under Article 17-18 LIS with secondary adjustments on the repatriated excess. Penalties under Article 196 LGT for non-presentation or incorrect TP documentation range from EUR 1,500 to EUR 22,000 per data set. Incorrect valuation causing harm may trigger a penalty of 15%-35% of the tax base adjusted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and TP signatories are personally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties derived from false TP documentation. Criminal liability may arise for facilitating tax fraud if the intercompany pricing is knowingly fictitious. Directors can also be subject to commercial disqualification under Article 241 LSC and travel restrictions in cross-border investigation proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Spanish SL as a conduit that holds no real operational substance: no GPS-sealed trucking assets, no drivers, no Spanish customs licences, no local management, while routing EU and Latin American cash flows to a non-resident parent that lacks beneficial ownership and actual business functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Spanish GAAR (Article 15 LGT) to recharacterise the transactions; denial of DTA or EU Directive benefits under the principal-purpose test; additional assessment at the 25% IS rate plus penalty of 35% of the recharacterised tax base; possible dividend withholding of 19% on deemed constructive distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign treaty-relief certificates knowing the entity lacks economic substance may be jointly liable for the entire deficiency. In criminal proceedings, they can be charged as aiding tax evasion or money laundering; imprisonment, personal fines, prohibitions on contracting with Spanish public authorities, and freezing orders are available legal outcomes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large untraceable cash payments for cargo trucking services, facilitating customs bonded loads without opiate or goods declarations, routing freight fees through private accounts of directors, failing to verify beneficial owners of subcontractors, or cooperating with criminal gangs to move tainted freight under customs seals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML Law 10/2010 imposes fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious and very serious violations; proportional fines up to the value of the laundered assets are permitted. Criminal money laundering under Articles 301-304 Criminal Code carries imprisonment and fines per transaction. Customs fraud involving commercial bonded operations can additionally trigger seizure of trucks and disciplinary action on the customs licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: All directors and ultimate beneficial owners can be prosecuted as money laundering co-perpetrators, especially if the company lacks a named AML compliance officer and fails to adopt internal controls. Personal liability includes civil recovery of illicit proceeds, travel bans, confiscation of personal and corporate assets, disqualification from transport licensing, and imprisonment for up to six years per laundering operation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Non-Filing of Corporate Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file Modelo 200, Modelo 202, Modelo 216, Modelo 232, or not filing Modelo 296 for dividends paid to non-resident owners despite statutory obligation; repeated defaults while distributing cash to shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Extemporaneous surcharge under Article 27 LGT of 5%-20% plus late interest; fixed penalties under Article 198 LGT of EUR 200 per omitted form, rising to EUR 20,000 where the AEAT previously noticed the obligation; sanctions for not filing information returns of 20% of the amounts not disclosed, with a minimum EUR 300.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate liabilities and penalties if they knowingly failed to cause compliance. Persistent non-filing can be treated as criminal tax resistance, subject to fines and restraint measures; directors may also be barred from serving on any Spanish board until the debt is satisfied.
